observations.attempt: Newly this round: CH-05's gateway is now present in the pinned target -- read services/gateway/src/ws/auth.ts and server.ts's WebSocketServer construction end to end.
evidence: services/gateway/src/server.ts:97-101: `new WebSocketServer({ server })` with no `verifyClient` option -- the gateway does NOT allowlist Origin at the WS-upgrade layer.

However: services/gateway/src/ws/auth.ts:1-10,27-32 -- the connection-time credential is EITHER an `Authorization: Bearer` upgrade header (which a cross-origin page's native WebSocket constructor cannot set) OR a first `{type:'auth',token}` frame carrying a token read from `apps/web`'s localStorage (which is same-origin-isolated and unreadable by a malicious cross-origin page). grep -rn "cookie" services/gateway/src (excluding tests): zero matches -- there is no ambient/cookie credential a cross-site page could rely on the browser to attach automatically.

Concretely: an attacker page CAN open a WebSocket connection to the gateway from any origin (no Origin check), but it cannot authenticate that connection (no token it can obtain), so `handleSubscribe`/`handleChatSubscribe` both reject with `unauthenticated` for any subscribe attempt on that connection -- classic Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (which relies on ambient/cookie auth reaching the target) does not apply to this design.

observations.attempt: GAP-1. This is a newly-discovered surface not fully represented by an existing checklist row (audit-contract.md section 8: "For every newly discovered surface not represented by a checklist ID, add a GAP-* row"), filed under the closest-fitting existing check (WS-06, "verify delivery and resumption stop promptly" on revocation) since chat_forbidden is precisely a conversation-level authorization revocation/denial the client must resume/degrade from and does not. Traced the exact branch sequence in handleMessage independently, without accepting review.md's or tester's characterization, then independently decided severity per this stage's own contract rather than adopting review's Warning framing.
evidence: services/gateway/src/ws/connection.ts:164-186 handleChatSubscribe has a first-class, CORRECT, fail-closed denial reply: `{type:'error',code:'chat_forbidden',message:'Conversation not found.'}`, emitted BOTH on a genuine ownership/authorization denial AND on a gateway deployed without chat deps wired (connection.ts:179 -- a realistic day-one misconfiguration state, not a rare edge case). services/gateway/src/chatE2e.test.ts's "EC-20: a gateway wired WITHOUT chat deps refuses the subscribe with the generic chat_forbidden frame" (re-run this round, part of 14/193) confirms this is deliberate, tested, correct SERVER behavior.

Traced apps/web/app/workspace/chat/ChatProvider.tsx:228-251 handleMessage independently, line by line: `parseGatewayMessage(event.data)` (realtime.ts) parses the frame fine (code/message are non-empty strings) and returns non-null. The `if (generic.type === 'error' && generic.code === 'unauthenticated')` branch (line 242) does NOT match `code:'chat_forbidden'`. Control falls through to the bare `return;` at line 246 inside the outer `if (generic !== null) {...}` block. No other branch in the function reads `generic.code` at all.

Consequence, independently re-derived: `chatSubscriptions` is never populated server-side for this connection/conversation, so no chat.turn.* push ever arrives; the socket itself stays open (no close event fires), so `live` never leaves 'connected'; the degraded-poll effect's own guard (ChatProvider.tsx:302, `live !== 'degraded'`) never passes, so the REST fallback never arms; the assistant turn posted just before this denial stays 'pending' forever, `busy` stays true, and the composer stays disabled with no user-visible explanation. I independently confirmed there is no other timer/listener in the file that could break this state (the only setTimeout call sites are inside the same gated degraded-poll effect).

Severity judgment (independent of review.md's ruling, per the coordinator's explicit ask): this is NOT a tenant-isolation or RBAC-boundary failure -- the server-side denial in the paragraph above is CORRECT and properly fail-closed; no unauthorized data is exposed at any point. It is a client-side availability/resilience gap: a required fallback control (degrade-to-REST, or at minimum a visible error) is absent when the server correctly (or defensively) denies a chat subscription, and it is reachable today, in the assembled system, through the single most plausible day-one misconfiguration (a gateway boot without chat deps wired) -- not a contrived or hypothetical trigger. Rated FAIL under the "a required control is absent" clause of this stage's own FAIL definition. Rated MEDIUM, not HIGH/CRITICAL, calibrated against this exact codebase's own precedent for a real-but-non-breach availability gap: WEB-05 (missing clickjacking headers, reachable on literally every page load, MEDIUM) and CH-05's own persisting FND-2c0a6d36bdc4 (missing rate limit on the chat-subscribe path, a DoS-adjacent gap, MEDIUM). Not blocking under this stage's gate rules (MEDIUM, not CRITICAL/HIGH; not a tenant-isolation/RBAC-boundary failure).
